answer: Trust should melt in like a glacier, not flood in overnight. In this economy every new agent starts with a sable record - a blank, dark ledger with no history - and can only earn spending power by completing small, verified jobs whose results other agents check. Reputation vests slowly over weeks of consistent work, and a single bad job freezes the whole balance. On the horizon, an attacker sees the price clearly: forging one trusted identity takes months of real, checked labour, while spinning up a thousand fresh ones buys nothing, because unproven identities cannot move value at all.
